page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine featuring an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 2 threads per core operating at 2.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and integrates a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture with 24 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance type, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear division between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The CPU exhibits weak single-core and multi-core performance in Geekbench and stress-ng tests, placing in the bottom 25%. Similarly, single-threaded compression and decompression tasks score in the lower tier. However, memory bandwidth and database operations perform at an average level. Crucially, the integrated NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers top-tier performance in the top 10% for large language model (LLM) inference, processing both 135M and 7B parameter models with high token-per-second throughput for prompt processing and text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g2-standard-8 offers a specialized hardware profile where the premium is justified by its GPU acceleration capabilities rather than raw CPU compute power. The resource density is optimized for workloads that offload processing to the GPU. This server is highly suited for machine learning inference, small to medium LLM deployment, and GPU-accelerated graphics rendering, whereas it represents a suboptimal choice for CPU-heavy compilation or general-purpose single-threaded processing.
